knownGaps.rationale: The app registers Aurelia's exported ArrayLikeHandler and the TypeChecker knows ArrayLike<ScopeTask>, but repeatability projection consults only the built-in resolver categories, emits a false AUR0777, and degrades the repeat local to unknown.

The project-local context-scope controller explicitly activates its view with Scope.fromParent(parent, value), but semantic-runtime treats app-owned template controllers as pass-through: the child value binding context is missing and the valid explicit parent lookup silently resolves no symbol, with no open-scope seam.

The app registers an IRepeatableHandler for TaskWindow, but repeat projection ignores the open registration fact, emits a confident AUR0777 and downstream TS18046, and reports complete closure instead of preserving an admitted source with unknown element type.

The parser emits ObjectBindingPattern for repeat.for object syntax, while the checked-in Repeat controller only materializes ArrayDestructuring/ObjectDestructuring and therefore creates no locals. Semantic-runtime currently accepts and types the non-working syntax without a diagnostic.

Raw AUR0777, assignment, checker, and weak-slot rows are all grounded evidence and must remain available. Presentation lacks an explicit causal edge from the rejected iterator projection to its derived repeat-local diagnostics, so the IDE still presents six consequences as independent problems instead of contextual evidence under the two root errors.

Framework With substitutes an empty object only for undefined; null becomes the child binding context and later scope lookup can throw. Semantic-runtime erases null with getNonNullableType and reports the reachable runtime hazard as clean.

Aurelia's nullable flag changes the runtime coercer wrapper, but semantic-runtime collapses type coercion to setterKind=type-coercion and drops nullable from both BindableDefinition and the public resource row.
CustomAttributeDefinition retains noMultiBindings and template lowering honors it, but SemanticResourceDefinitionRow does not project the policy for MCP, IDE, or future AOT consumers.

The framework accepts set: String as a closed bindable interceptor, but semantic-runtime classifies the global function reference as open through both decorator and static-record metadata while inline function expressions close.

Resource definition rows preserve bindable value type and call-signature facts, but SemanticTemplateCursorBindableRow drops them before hover and other cursor consumers can present the selected bindable's type.

Aurelia executes arbitrary IAttrMapper.useTwoWay predicates against the live element. Semantic-runtime now rejects partially understood predicate conjunctions instead of widening them, but does not yet preserve an executable or open predicate product, so the valid live-attribute branch remains conservatively to-view.
